name: Cloak-room check: put a steep low-pass last on the master to audition only the club-wall low end, diagnose kick-only vs masking mush vs clear priorities, then balance kick (reference) and bass with simple low and mid shelves while the check stays on
goal: Judge and fix low-end storytelling with one listening trick and simple shelves: a master low-pass ('cloak-room check') isolates what a club subwoofer will exaggerate, revealing whether the low end is kick-only (too separated), a masking mush (no danceable pulse), or a clear priority groove. Then, with the check still on, leave the kick as reference and use shelf filters to set the bass's low band vs the kick and its mid band vs the other mids — prefer less processing over multiband heroics. Delta vs mix/bass clusters: the named cloak-room listening protocol and the three failure modes, plus shelf-only balancing under that filter rather than solo-EQ or multiband ducking alone.

source.title: Why your low end sounds amateur (maybe)

prerequisites: DAW with a master low-pass (steep) and per-track low/high shelves or a two-shelf EQ
Kick and bass (and other low contributors) in the session

inputs.name: mix
inputs.description: Full mix including kick and bass

outputs.name: balanced_low_end
outputs.description: Low end with clear kick/bass priorities that still grooves as a whole

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Do the check as the last device on the master (or a safe audition chain), not as the only way you ever listen.
Masking is allowed; clear priority beats sterile separation.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.
Steady pitch: leave out intentional pitch-drift LFOs unless the brief asks for tape wobble (Matt prefers steady pitch).

steps.action: Insert a low-pass filter as the last thing on the master (or an audition bus). Sweep it so you mainly hear the sub/low body — the 'cloak-room check' (what you hear queuing outside the club).
steps.expect: Low end isolated; mids/highs no longer distract

steps.action: With the check on, A/B your low end against three failure modes: (A) kick-only / overly separated (amateur 'just kicks'), (B) everything masking everything (bass buries the kick; no danceable story), (C) clear priorities that still blend and groove as one part. Aim for C.
Treat bass as having both a low band and a mid band (and sometimes highs). You will balance those bands separately with shelves, not as one fader.

Solo or focus the kick under the cloak-room check; leave its level as the reference. Bring the bass in and use a low shelf to set its sub/low body against the kick until the kick stays readable but the bass has weight.
steps.expect: Kick remains the pulse; bass has weight

steps.action: Still under the check (or briefly off for mids): use a mid/upper shelf on the bass to sit its harmonic body against other mid elements without needing multiband or parallel tricks. Prefer the simplest shelf moves that get priorities clear.
steps.expect: Bass mid body fits the mix

steps.action: Remove or bypass the cloak-room filter and confirm the full mix still grooves; accept a little masking if the story is clear.
steps.expect: Club-safe low end with clear priorities

verification: Under the master LPF, kick and bass priorities are obvious.
Bass low shelf vs kick keeps the pulse danceable.
Full-range mix does not rely on extreme multiband to sound balanced.
